title: workload.json of the tool-using agent Track
description: The whole shape of a Workload declaration of the agentic Track. Requiredness is split (ADR 0002, clarification of 2026-11-04). The schema requires the keys every entry point reads. It does not require `question`, `objective`, `limitations` or `primary_criterion` (read by `init`, which refuses their absence with DECLARATION_INCOMPLETE), `scenarios` (the technical scenarios of the `scripted_fixture` Mode), `answer_schema` (read only by the scripted fixture) a Partition under `cases` (read by the entry points that need that Partition), or `database` (a Workload whose data lives outside the repository declares a data manifest instead, `data-manifest.json` beside this file; `run agent` refuses a Workload without `database` with DATABASE_NOT_DECLARED, and `data verify` refuses one that declares both with DATA_DECLARED_TWICE): each of those entry points refuses the key's absence, with a code, in Track code. The rule that a Configuration may extend only a declared Configuration, without a cycle, relates values to each other and stays in Track code (hypotrail.agentic.declaration).

primary_criterion.description: The Criterion that is the primary one of an Assessment of this Workload (CMP-03). It is one of the Criteria of the Scorer chinook_contract_v1, or text_facts_success, the primary Criterion of text_facts_v1; the Study freezes it as its primary metric.

cases.description: The file of the Cases of each Partition role. The roles are the Track's (hypotrail.agentic.partitions); a Workload cannot add one.

scoring_config.description: The Scorer config file a Scorer reads from the Study, as `init` publishes it; it enters the Protocol digest.

resampling.description: The resampling unit and seed of the paired interval on the delta of a Comparison: `case` draws Cases, `group` draws whole groups of Cases, and every Case then declares its `group`. The level and the count of resamples are the core's (hypotrail.core.intervals). Optional: a Workload without it gets no interval.

configuration.description: Either a full system text, or another Configuration's text followed by one added instruction.
